title: Consent-windowed anonymization and staged erasure workflow for console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a privacy-first analytics retention mechanism that enforces user consent windows and performs staged transformations (mask -> redact -> hard delete) across our console usage pipelines. This ticket scopes the backend adapters, schema flags, erasure orchestration, metrics, and audit trail necessary to support per-customer and per-event retention policies without breaking downstream OLAP and alerting consumers.

Goals:
- Respect consent_version and consent_granularity on events; allow per-customer retention windows set via Console.
- Implement staged erasure: 1) PII masking (near real-time), 2) schematized anonymization for derived analytics, 3) irreversible deletion of raw payloads after retention expiry.
- Maintain provable audit logs (immutable entries) for compliance evidence.
- Minimize disruption to analytics pipelines and keep queryability for aggregated dashboards.

Non-goals:
- Full customer-facing deletion UI (handled by separate PM ticket).
- Re-architecting storage layer; we will implement as adapters atop existing event store and materialized views.

Design proposal (high-level):
- Event schema additions: add fields on each ingested event: pii_flags (list), consent_version (string), retention_window_end (iso-date), anonymization_state (enum: RAW | MASKED | ANONYMIZED | DELETED).
- Ingest adapters: enrich events at intake with retention_window_end computed from customer policy (from Config API). If user has revocation event, set retention_window_end = now + grace_period = 0 for immediate masking path.
- Nearline processor (KStream consumer): responsible for initial PII masking within 30s of event receipt. Masking is deterministic where possible (hash with customer-scoped salt from KMS) so derived pipelines can still join on hashed IDs when allowed.
- Batch anonymizer job: nightly job that reads events eligible for anonymization (past masking grace but before deletion window) and runs structured column removal + generalization to preserve aggregate fidelity. Produces a versioned snapshot to materialized views.
- Erasure worker: queued, rate-limited job that performs irreversible deletion from primary raw store and updates anonymization_state -> DELETED and writes an immutable audit row to the AuditDB containing proof metadata (job id, timestamp, hashes of removed object ids).
- Audit & evidence: every state transition writes an immutable audit record (append-only) and links to the customer config and policy version. Retention of audit records follows legal guidance (separate retention, longer than event retention).

Trade-offs / rationale:
- Deterministic hashing vs full tokenization: hashing preserves ability to measure DAU/MAU across pipeline stages but retains risk of re-identification if salt leaks. We will use per-customer KMS-managed salts and rotate salts with migration jobs.
- Staged approach increases pipeline complexity but reduces breakage to downstream aggregations and customer SLAs. Immediate hard delete would lower our forensic ability and increase metric regressions.
- Doing masking in nearline vs at ingest: nearline gives us consistency and allows the raw store to retain original for short debugging windows (configurable by customer).

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Schema & config: add event fields, Config API extension to expose per-customer retention policy. (ENG, PM, Security) — 2d
2) KMS salt API: implement customer-scoped salt storage and retrieval with IAM checks (Security/Infra) — 3d
3) Nearline masker: KStream consumer to perform deterministic masking and set anonymization_state = MASKED. Add metrics and tracing. (ENG) — 4d
4) Nightly anonymizer: batch job to generalize columns and update materialized views. (ENG/Data) — 3d
5) Erasure worker & audit: implement worker to delete raw objects, write audit evidence, and emit events for downstream consumers. (ENG/Security) — 4d
6) Dashboards & alerts: add SLOs for masking latency, deletion completion, and audit delivery. (Observability) — 2d
7) Privacy review & legal signoff: deliver design doc, threat model, and test plan. (Security/Legal) — concurrent

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingested events show retention_window_end and are masked within 30s for customers with masking enabled.
- Nightly anonymizer produces materialized views without PII fields and dashboard deltas <2% compared to pre-anonymized baselines for key metrics.
- Erasure worker completes deletion within configured SLA (default 7 days post retention expiry) and audit records are present for every deleted object.
- End-to-end integration tests (simulated customer) and a small pilot with internal customers.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for masking transforms and KMS salt usage.
- Local integration with a test Kafka and S3-backed raw store.
- E2E staging run with synthetic dataset and dashboard regression checks.
- Privacy fuzz tests: attempt to re-identify hashed values with multiple salts.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRIV/Consent-windowed+anonymization+design
- Proto schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/events-proto/pull/42
- Nearline masker PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/pipeline/pull/1101
- KMS salt proposal: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Sec/KMS+customer+salt+proposal
- Compliance checklist: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/REDACTED

Progress updates (chronological):
- 2025-03-01: Ticket created. Aligned with PM on scope; decided to implement deterministic masking + KMS salt rotation rather than tokenization for MVP.
- 2025-03-02: Proto schema change approved by Data infra; updated ingest lambda to carry retention_window_end.
- 2025-03-03: KMS salt storage prototype complete; needs IAM gating. Security to review.
- 2025-03-04: Nearline masker initial consumer committed; unit tests pass locally. Integration tests failing due to Kafka ACLs in staging.
- 2025-03-05: Blocker: staging Kafka ACLs prevent masker from subscribing to the privacy topic. Raised INF-6123 and requested access.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal: required retention of audit evidence vs customer deletion timeframes. Working with Legal for minimum windows.
- Infra: need cross-region KMS key access for customers with data residency; current KMS infra needs extension.
- Operational cost: hashing and anonymization jobs increase CPU/IO. We need an estimate of steady-state cost for 1000 customers.

Next steps:
- Resolve Kafka ACL INF-6123 (blocked).
- Security review of KMS salt access pattern and rotation plan.
- Run pilot with 3 internal customers and validate dashboard regressions.
